messages.text:
For the first batch, we propose giving one external color specialist access to the master images. Seeing the full page helps the specialist distinguish a color cast in the scan from variation in the paper. We would name the specialist for your written approval, bind them to the same confidentiality terms as the studio, and give them view-only access through an individual account with downloads disabled. Access would end when calibration is complete or five calendar days after the first batch is scanned, whichever comes first. If full-page access is unacceptable, would you approve crops showing the color target and representative areas of paper and ink, with no readable text?

Within the studio, only the assigned scanning and quality-control staff would have access. We propose keeping working files for ten calendar days after delivery of each batch so you can flag defects and we can correct them. We would delete the working files on day ten. If a correction is still open, we would ask for written approval to keep only the affected files until an agreed date. Encrypted backups would expire within 45 calendar days of working-file deletion, with access restricted to staff responsible for disaster recovery. If a backup is restored during that period, we would reapply the deletion before returning the system to use.

We would also like to publish one process photograph showing the scanner setup and color target. We would frame it to exclude letter text, handwriting, names and archive labels, and send you the exact image, caption and proposed publication channel for written approval before use.

Please include the following terms in the pilot schedule.

- **Specialist access.** We will supply a calibration sheet for the full-page color check and identify the two restricted collections before scanning. For those collections, the specialist may see only the calibration sheet. For other collections, if the sheet leaves a color question unresolved, we can approve specific masked crops showing the target and representative paper or ink. The crops must conceal handwriting and identifying details even where no text is readable. The archive must approve both the named specialist and the crops in writing before access. We accept your confidentiality, individual-account, view-only and download controls, with access ending at calibration or five calendar days after the first batch is scanned, whichever comes first. Master images stay with the assigned studio scanning and quality-control staff.
- **Retention and deletion.** We accept ten calendar days after each batch delivery for working files, including crops. An open correction requires prior written approval identifying the affected files and a firm deletion date. Please keep pilot images out of backups if feasible. If that is infeasible, specify the shortest backup expiry you can support and whether it differs for the restricted collections. The proposed 45-day backup period remains an outstanding exception requiring written agreement. Any agreed backup exception must include your encryption, disaster-recovery access restrictions and re-deletion on restore. Please provide a dated deletion record for each batch identifying what was deleted, any approved hold and its expiry, followed by confirmation when the last backup copy expires.
- **Incident contact.** Before transfer, both parties will enter a monitored incident email and phone number in the schedule. The studio must notify the archive through those contacts promptly, within 24 hours of discovering suspected loss, unauthorized access or disclosure, and provide updates on affected materials and containment.
- **Publicity.** You may submit one equipment-only photograph taken with all collection materials, labels, screens displaying collection information, and the color target out of frame. Publication requires our prior written approval of the exact image, caption and channel. Any reuse in another channel requires fresh approval.

Please confirm whether the calibration sheet and approved crops will support the pilot, and whether you can exclude pilot images from backups.

The calibration sheet and approved crops will support the pilot. For the two restricted collections you identify before scanning, the specialist will see only the sheet. If it leaves a color question unresolved, our assigned staff will check the master internally. For other collections, we will submit a specific masked crop only when the sheet leaves a question unresolved. Each crop will conceal handwriting and identifying details, including marks that could identify a donor even when the text is unreadable.

We will obtain your written approval of the named specialist before granting access and of each crop before showing it. The specialist will be bound by the studio’s confidentiality terms and use an individual, view-only account with downloads disabled. Access will end at calibration completion or five calendar days after the first batch is scanned, whichever comes first. Only assigned studio scanning and quality-control staff will have access to masters for production work.

We cannot yet confirm that pilot images can be excluded from backups. Our current backup rotation is 45 days for all collections, including the two restricted collections. If exclusion is feasible, we will use it. Otherwise, the shortest expiry we can commit to is 45 calendar days after working-file deletion. We will confirm the outcome before transfer and proceed with any affected collection only if you agree to the exception in writing. Under that exception, backups will be encrypted, access will be limited to staff responsible for disaster recovery, and we will reapply deletions before returning a restored system to use.

We will delete working files, including crops, ten calendar days after each batch delivery. To retain files for an open correction, we will first obtain written approval identifying the files and a firm deletion date. For each batch, we will provide a dated record identifying the files deleted, any approved hold and its expiry. We will update the record when held files are deleted and, where backups apply, confirm when the last backup copy expires.

Before transfer, we will enter our monitored incident email and phone number alongside yours. We will notify you through those contacts promptly and within 24 hours of discovering suspected loss, unauthorized access or disclosure, then provide updates on affected materials and containment.

We accept the equipment-only photograph terms. We will keep all collection materials, labels, screens displaying collection information and the color target out of frame. We will publish only with your prior written approval of the exact photograph, caption and channel, and obtain fresh written approval for any other channel.

Please add a color-validation step to the schedule. The specialist can check the scanner using the calibration sheet and an archive-approved masked image of a comparison sheet. Only the masked version of the comparison sheet may leave the archive. If masking obscures a feature needed to judge color, we can arrange supervised review of the comparison original at the archive one morning next week, without photography or copying.

We propose that the specialist report on scanner calibration, assigned studio quality-control staff check the donor scans internally, and our conservator give final written color approval against the originals. The specialist receives no donor letters or donor-letter images, including crops. This replaces the earlier crop permission.

Calibration can proceed now. Once the incident contacts are recorded and backup exclusion is confirmed or an exception is approved in writing for the affected collection, the studio may scan a first batch for the conservator’s review. Please wait for written color approval before scanning further batches on that setup.

Keep the agreed deletion clock tied to delivery. Delete working files ten calendar days after each batch is delivered, even if color review is pending, unless we approve a correction hold in writing for named files through a firm deletion date. Delete the masked comparison image when calibration ends or the five-day specialist access window closes, whichever comes first, and record its deletion. The proposed 45-day backup period after working-file deletion remains an outstanding exception requiring written approval. Please retain the agreed batch deletion records and confirmation of final backup expiry.

Can you validate the setup from the masked comparison image, or should we reserve the supervised morning? Please confirm that your team can work to the first-batch approval and deletion terms above.

Please reserve the supervised morning next week. The first masked test obscured an ink-tone feature the specialist needs to verify calibration. We can begin with the calibration sheet now, then have the approved specialist inspect that feature on the nonrestricted comparison original at the archive, under supervision and without photography or copying. Only the archive-approved masked version may leave the archive. We will delete it and record the deletion when calibration ends or the five-day specialist access window closes, whichever comes first.

We accept the first-batch approval and deletion terms. The specialist will report on scanner calibration and will have no access to donor letters or donor-letter images, including crops. Once the incident contacts are recorded and backup exclusion is confirmed or an exception is approved in writing for the affected collection, we can scan the first batch. Our assigned quality-control staff will check the scans internally. We will wait for the conservator’s written color approval against the originals before scanning another batch on that setup.

For any rescan, we propose that the operator reopen the delivered replacement file before deleting the working copy, verify that it is the correct page, and check that the reported defect has been corrected. For an ink-tone defect, we ask the conservator to check the specific feature against the original and confirm acceptance in writing. Can we add that test to the schedule?

The test will run within the existing ten-calendar-day period from batch delivery. A rescan will not restart the clock. If acceptance is pending near the deadline, we will request a written hold naming the affected files and a firm deletion date. Without approval by the deadline, we will delete on schedule. We will provide the dated batch deletion record, record any approved hold and its eventual deletion, and confirm final backup expiry wherever a backup exception has been agreed. The proposed 45-day exception still requires your written approval.

Agreed. Please add the rescan test to the signed schedule. The operator will reopen the delivered replacement file, verify that it is the correct page and check the reported defect. For an ink-tone correction, our conservator will compare the specific feature with the original and confirm acceptance in writing.

We’ll arrange the supervised morning next week and confirm the date and time with you. Calibration may begin now using the calibration sheet. The approved specialist may inspect the comparison original at the archive under supervision, without photography or copying, and will report on scanner calibration. Only the approved masked comparison image may leave the archive. Please delete it and record deletion when calibration ends or the agreed five-day access window closes, whichever comes first. The specialist may see no donor letters or donor-letter images, including crops.

First-batch scanning may proceed once both incident contacts are recorded and backup exclusion is confirmed or we approve an exception in writing for the affected collection. Assigned studio staff will check the scans internally. Further batches on that setup require the conservator’s written color approval against the originals.

Delete working files ten calendar days after batch delivery. A rescan or pending acceptance does not extend that deadline. Any correction hold requires our written approval by the deadline, naming the files and a firm deletion date. Please provide the dated batch deletion record, update it when held files are deleted, and confirm final backup expiry wherever an exception applies. The proposed 45-day backup period after working-file deletion remains the sole outstanding exception.
